title: Creating Agents that Co-Create — Karina Nguyen, OpenAI

primary.label: AI Product, UX & Human Factors
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 48%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on product design lessons, human-AI collaboration, trust, and co-creation across Canvas, ChatGPT, and Claude rather than on model internals or agent architecture. The talk spans general AI product design with emphasis on creative co-creation, individual productivity tools, and coding assistance. The talk progresses from research on scaling paradigms through current product features to a future vision of co-innovation interfaces. Prerequisites include familiarity with pre-training, RL, and Chain of Thought, indicating an intermediate-level audience. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer Summit 2025 in New York. All claims are grounded in transcript excerpts with grade said_in_transcript.

summary: Karina Nguyen, an AI researcher at OpenAI formerly at Anthropic (where she worked on Claude for about two years), presents two major scaling paradigms transforming frontier product research. The first is next token prediction (pre-training), a world-building machine where models learn physics and causality by predicting the next token. Some tasks like translation are easy to learn during pre-training, while math, spatial reasoning, and creative writing are harder, requiring more compute or Chain of Thought. The 2020-2021 pre-training era, exemplified by GitHub Copilot, used post-training (RLHF/RLAIF) to teach models code completion and diff prediction. The second paradigm, introduced with OpenAI's o1, is scaling reinforcement learning on Chain of Thought with more test-time compute, enabling complex reasoning. She envisions agents (reasoning + tool use + long context) as the current stage and co-innovators (agents plus creativity via human-AI collaboration) as the next. These paradigms unlock rapid product cycles: distillation, synthetic data generation, new RL environments with tools like browsing and canvas, and in-context learning. Design lessons include bringing unfamiliar capabilities into familiar form factors (100K context via file uploads) and building modular compositions that scale with model capabilities (ChatGPT Tasks). In the latter portion, she explores bridging real-time interaction to asynchronous task completion (models going off for hours to research or write code), with trust as the key bottleneck, solvable through collaborative affordances for verification and real-time feedback. Claude in Slack was an early virtual teammate prototype. Canvas, her first project at OpenAI, is a flexible interface serving as co-creator, co-editor, pair programmer, and data scientist—scaling to multiplayer and multi-agent collaboration. She envisions personalized multimodal tutors adapting to learning styles, generative entertainment on the fly, and non-technical people creating and deploying their own tools. The future of internet access shifts from clicking links to accessing through models' lens with personalized multimodal outputs (e.g., 3D interactive solar system visualizations). The ultimate vision is a blank canvas that self-morphs to user intent—becoming an IDE for coders or a novel-writing toolkit for writers—and co-innovation through creative co-direction with highly reasoning agentic systems to create new novels, films, games, science, and knowledge.

sections.title: Introduction and Overview
sections.summary: Karina Nguyen introduces herself as an AI researcher at OpenAI, formerly at Anthropic working on Claude. She previews the talk: two scaling paradigms in AI research, vignettes from building Claude and ChatGPT, design challenges, and the future of agents evolving from collaborators to co-innovators.

sections.title: First Scaling Paradigm: Next Token Prediction (Pre-training)
sections.summary: Explains next token prediction as a world-building machine where models learn physics and causality by predicting the next token. Some tasks (translation) are easy, while math, spatial reasoning, and creative writing are hard. Creative writing is especially difficult because it requires world-building, storytelling, and plot coherence over long sequences. Compute scaling is critical for harder tasks, requiring Chain of Thought.

sections.title: Post-Training Era and GitHub Copilot
sections.summary: The 2020-2021 era focused on scaling pre-training. GitHub Copilot exemplifies this, using post-training (RLHF/RLAIF) to teach models to complete function bodies, generate multi-line completions, and predict/apply diffs. Much remains to be explored in post-training for code reasoning.

sections.title: Second Scaling Paradigm: RL on Chain of Thought (o1)
sections.summary: OpenAI's o1 model introduced scaling reinforcement learning on Chain of Thought, using more test-time compute. The model learns to think during training and learns from RL feedback signals. Enables solving harder tasks like medical problems. Raises research questions about faithfulness of Chain of Thought and backtracking.

sections.title: New Interaction Paradigm and Agents
sections.summary: The new interaction paradigm where models think for long periods creates design challenges. One approach: streaming model thoughts to users with summarized communication. This year is the year of agents—complex reasoning with tools (browsing, search, computer use) over long horizons. The next stage is co-innovators: agents plus creativity enabled through human-AI collaboration.

sections.title: Product Research Unlocked by Scaling Paradigms
sections.summary: The scaling paradigms unlock rapid product evaluation cycles: distilling reasoning models to smaller models, generating synthetic data for new post-training and RL environments, creating new task classes (e.g., multiplayer collaboration simulation), using more complex RL environments with tools like canvas, and leveraging in-context learning for rapid developer iteration.

sections.title: Design Vignettes: Familiar Form Factors and ChatGPT Tasks
sections.summary: Shares lessons from Anthropic and OpenAI. 100K context succeeded because it was deployed via familiar file uploads rather than infinite chat. ChatGPT Tasks takes the familiar concept of reminders/scheduling and scales it with model capabilities—daily stories, searches, multimodal language learning. Key lesson: product features should enable modular compositions that scale with future model capabilities.

sections.title: Bridging Real-Time to Async, Trust, and Claude in Slack
sections.summary: Envisions bridging real-time interaction to asynchronous task completion, where models go off for hours to research or write code. Trust is the key bottleneck, solvable through collaborative affordances for verification and real-time feedback enabling model self-improvement. Claude in Slack was Anthropic's first virtual teammate prototype, leveraging Slack's affordances for tools, image uploads, and multiplayer collaboration. ChatGPT Tasks was inspired by Claude in Slack prototypes that summarized channels every Friday.

sections.title: Canvas as Flexible Co-Creation Interface
sections.summary: Canvas was her first project at OpenAI—a flexible interface enabling fine-grained editing as co-creator and co-editor, with search for report generation and output verification. The interface scales to multiplayer (others joining documents) and multi-agent collaboration (model critics or editors). Also envisions personalized multimodal tutors adapting to learning styles (visual vs auditory). Shares anecdote of using Canvas on a plane to create a game as generative entertainment on the fly.

sections.title: Canvas as Pair Programmer and Data Scientist
sections.summary: Canvas enables non-technical people to create and deploy their own tools and apps for the first time. It functions as a pair programmer because it was trained for collaborative writing and coding, with search tools for API documentation. It can also serve as a data scientist, generating real-time analysis from uploaded CSV documents.

sections.title: Research Co-Creation and New Knowledge
sections.summary: Excitement around helping models become better at research and creating new knowledge. Demonstrates co-creating a document reproducing a co-published paper interactively, leveraging the model's internal knowledge. Envisions humans and AI working together to propose new research hypotheses and verify directions, delegating tasks to AI assistants.

sections.title: Future: Invisible Software, Internet Through Models' Lens, and Co-Innovation
sections.summary: Envisions a layer of invisible software creation for all, where people create tools from mobile devices. Internet access shifts from clicking links to accessing through models' lens with personalized multimodal outputs (e.g., 3D interactive solar system visualizations). The ultimate interface is a blank canvas that self-morphs to user intent—becoming an IDE for coders or generating novel-writing tools on the fly. Co-innovation happens through creative co-direction with highly reasoning agentic systems to create new novels, films, games, science, and knowledge.
